title: SPIRE: Spin-Resolved Particle-in-Cell with Radiative Corrections for Extreme Laser--Plasma Interactions
abstract: We present SPIRE, a spin- and photon-polarization-resolved particle-in-cell (PIC) code for self-consistent simulations of laser-plasma interactions in the strong-field quantum electrodynamics (QED) regime. The classical PIC framework combines a Yee-grid finite-difference time-domain Maxwell solver, a relativistic Boris particle pusher, shape-function particle-grid interpolation, Esirkepov charge-conserving current deposition, laser boundary injection, and a relativistic moving window in one, two, and three spatial dimensions. A vectorial Laguerre-Gaussian laser injector based on an angular-spectrum formulation supports tightly focused, nonparaxial optical orbital-angular-momentum modes. The strong-field QED module treats nonlinear Compton scattering and nonlinear Breit-Wheeler pair production as stochastic processes using spin- and polarization-resolved probabilities in the local constant-field approximation. Electron and positron spin evolution includes stochastic transitions, no-emission corrections, and Thomas-Bargmann-Michel-Telegdi precession with a field-dependent anomalous magnetic moment. Photon polarization is represented by the Stokes vector and evolves through nonlinear Compton scattering, pair production, vacuum birefringence, and vacuum dichroism. The implementation is verified with one-, two-, and three-dimensional benchmarks. Classical PIC results are cross-checked against SMILEI, and the spin- and polarization-resolved QED modules reproduce published results for polarized electron generation, vacuum birefringence and dichroism, and dense polarized positron production. These benchmarks verify the coupled classical PIC, strong-field QED, spin, and photon-polarization modules implemented in SPIRE.

summaries.en: SPIRE is a spin- and photon-polarization-resolved particle-in-cell code that self-consistently simulates extreme laser-plasma interactions in the strong-field QED regime, combining a classical PIC framework with stochastic nonlinear Compton scattering and Breit-Wheeler pair production, spin evolution, and Stokes-vector photon polarization dynamics.

title: Selective spatiotemporal mode-locking in multimode Mamyshev oscillators
abstract: Spatiotemporal mode-locking (STML) in multimode fibers introduces spatial degrees of freedom for ultrashort pulse generation, yet flexible manipulation of transverse mode compositions within multimode solitons remains challenging. Here, we propose a spectrum-to-mode mapping strategy in multimode Mamyshev oscillators (MOs) to selectively synchronize specific transverse modes through synergistic cross-phase modulation and offset spectral filtering. Meanwhile, four-wave mixing acts to stabilize intermodal phase relationships, facilitating selective STML characterized by diverse mode compositions with matched group velocities. Spatiotemporal solitons containing the pure LP01 mode, degenerate LP11 modes, or LP02+LP21 composite modes are selectively realized and mapped across the parameter space spanned by intracavity gain and filter detuning. Furthermore, intracavity collisions between coexisting mode groups with disparate group velocities are demonstrated to enable dynamic mode selection. Beyond the simulation of six modes in graded-index multimode fibers, selective STML is also demonstrated in MOs based on step-index multimode fibers and fibers supporting more transverse modes, confirming the generality of our approach. This strategy offers a versatile and robust pathway for transverse mode regulation and provides new insights into full dimensional structured light manipulation in multimode ultrafast fiber lasers.

summaries.en: This paper proposes a spectrum-to-mode mapping strategy in multimode Mamyshev oscillators that selectively synchronizes specific transverse modes via cross-phase modulation and offset spectral filtering, enabling spatiotemporal solitons with pure LP01, degenerate LP11, or LP02+LP21 mode compositions.

title: Inverse identification of thermal-radiative parameters for reduced effective-temperature uncertainty in an ion optical clock
abstract: The blackbody-radiation (BBR) shift remains a leading systematic uncertainty of room-temperature single-ion optical clocks. Accurate evaluation of this shift requires the effective temperature at the ion position, which is difficult because RF heating, low and spatially varying surface emissivity and inaccessible trap surfaces make this quantity difficult to measure directly. Here, we developed a hybrid inversion framework that combines radiance-domain infrared thermography, black-painted high-emissivity reference regions, a finite-element model of a 171Yb+ end-cap ion trap and a reduced-order surrogate for repeated forward calculations and parameter identification. The surrogate reproduced the FE test fields with a full-field mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.02220 mK. The calibrated model predicted the ion-position effective temperature with a combined standard uncertainty of 155.0 mK, corresponding to a temperature-related BBR frequency-shift uncertainty of 1.647 x 10^-19 for the 2S1/2-2F7/2 (467 nm) E3 transition. This method provides a reproducible route for reducing and tracing the BBR uncertainty of room-temperature trapped-ion optical clocks.

title: Multi-Objective Design of C-Shaped Targets for Energy--Divergence Control in Laser-Driven Proton Acceleration
abstract: We optimize the energy-divergence trade-off of laser-driven protons from a C-shaped target using two-dimensional particle-in-cell simulations and constrained multi-objective Bayesian optimization. Five geometry and focusing parameters are varied to maximize proton cutoff energy and minimize the RMS divergence of forward protons with E_k >= 5 MeV under a proton-only conversion-efficiency constraint of eta_H >= 9%. Of 82 designs, 60 are feasible and 15 Pareto-optimal. The Max-Energy and Min-Divergence endpoints yield 28.64 MeV at 52.51 degrees and 11.47 MeV at 11.13 degrees, respectively; a representative compromise yields 21.44 MeV at 38.44 degrees. Matched-stage diagnostics link these regimes to optical-field buildup, electron energization, charge separation, and outer-sheath organization. Numerical tests support the principal trends. Reflection timing does not support a monotonic trapping-duration law, and the charge-sheath relation remains non-local. These results establish a design-resolved route to controlling proton energy and angular quality.

summaries.en: Constrained multi-objective Bayesian optimization of two-dimensional particle-in-cell simulations for C-shaped targets identifies Pareto-optimal designs that trade off laser-driven proton cutoff energy against forward-proton divergence under a proton conversion-efficiency constraint.

title: Ultra-low-loss Ta2O5 waveguide for integrated nonlinear photonics
abstract: Integrated nonlinear photonics demands waveguides that simultaneously offer ultra-low-loss, relatively strong nonlinearity, and tight mode confinement. Tantalum pentoxide (Ta2O5) is attractive for this purpose because it combines a broad transparency window, relatively strong third-order nonlinearity, and favorable thick-film growth characteristics. In tightly confined Ta2O5 waveguides, however, enhanced interaction between the optical mode and etched sidewalls makes scattering loss an important limitation for achieving high Q anomalous-dispersion resonators. Here, we mitigate this confinement-scattering trade-off in pure Ta2O5 waveguides using a fabrication flow based on the Damascene concept. The resulting microring resonators (MRRs) with a cross-section of 1.6 {\mu}m x 0.85 {\mu}m exhibit intrinsic quality factors exceeding 4.0 x 106, corresponding to propagation losses below 10 dB/m, while maintaining anomalous dispersion suitable for bright dissipative Kerr soliton operation. Using these resonators, we generate a coherent bright single-soliton microcomb with a repetition rate of 108.32 GHz. Under optimized dual-pump operating conditions, the platform further exhibits an experimentally accessible single-soliton window spanning 7.5 GHz, indicating a large detuning tolerance for soliton operation; this broad operating window is consistent with the relatively weak thermo-optic response of Ta2O5. Thermal-bistability analysis further indicates that the residual scattering loss is comparable to the material-absorption loss, rather than dominating the loss budget. These results demonstrate that low optical loss, tight mode confinement, and dispersion engineering suitable for soliton formation can be jointly achieved in a pure Ta2O5 platform, providing an ultra-low-loss platform foundation for integrated nonlinear photonic devices and more complex chip-scale nonlinear photonic systems.

title: Plasma-neutral collision operators for hydrogen isotopes: kinetic and gyrokinetic descriptions, comparison to fluid
abstract: Plasma-neutral interactions critically affect the edge dynamics of magnetically confined fusion devices. Neutral atoms modify ion and electron velocity distributions, potentially affecting local instabilities Standard fluid models simplify these processes (namely charge exchange, ionization and recombination) using Maxwellian assumptions and linearized source terms. We revisit these assumptions for a hydrogen plasma interacting with hydrogen atoms. We derive plasma-neutral interaction terms in the kinetic and gyrokinetic frameworks. Accounting for velocity-dependent differential cross-sections, the model captures the kinetic impact of inelastic collisions on ions and electrons beyond energy and momentum exchange. We demonstrate that the fluid moments of the kinetic model reduce to standard fluid source terms under the appropriate assumptions of Maxwellianity and linearity. We compare the kinetic model with fluid models through their effects on distribution functions and fluid moments. Substantial discrepancies are observed, even for Maxwellian distributions. For charge exchange, the kinetic model yields momentum and energy exchange rates up to twice those predicted by fluid descriptions. We show that a fluid treatment of ionization greatly overestimates the mean kinetic energy of the produced electrons. These results highlight the limitations of fluid descriptions and the importance of kinetic effects in edge-plasma momentum and energy exchange.

summaries.en: Kinetic and gyrokinetic plasma-neutral collision operators for hydrogen isotopes reveal substantial discrepancies with fluid models, including up to twice the momentum and energy exchange rates for charge exchange and an overestimation of the mean kinetic energy of ionized electrons by fluid treatments.
summaries.zh: 针对氢同位素的动理学与回旋动理学等离子体-中性粒子碰撞算符显示，与流体模型存在显著差异，包括电荷交换的动量与能量交换率可高达流体预测的两倍，以及流体处理会高估电离产生电子的平均动能。

title: Resonant dispersive wave emission: a route toward few-cycle, tunable strong-field drivers in the visible
abstract: Intense ultrafast lasers are the backbone of strong-field physics and enable table-top scale applications of coherent high-photon energy radiation through high-harmonic generation (HHG). Using short-wavelength drivers in HHG promises highly efficient conversion into the extreme ultraviolet, but short pulse durations are essential to this approach. We generate multi-GW peak power, sub-10 fs pulses in the visible with broad spectral tunability (220--752 nm) by harnessing soliton dynamics in large-core, gas-filled capillary fibers for high-energy resonant dispersive wave emission. This establishes the potential of resonant dispersive waves as a new class of driving lasers for HHG and strong-field physics in addition to widespread applications in ultrafast spectroscopy.

summaries.en: By harnessing soliton dynamics in large-core, gas-filled capillary fibers, multi-GW peak power, sub-10 fs visible pulses with broad spectral tunability from 220 to 752 nm are generated via resonant dispersive wave emission, offering a new class of driving lasers for high-harmonic generation and strong-field physics.
summaries.zh: 通过利用大芯径充气毛细管光纤中的孤子动力学，基于共振色散波发射产生了峰值功率达多吉瓦、脉宽低于10飞秒且光谱可在220至752纳米范围内宽调谐的可见光脉冲，为高次谐波产生和强场物理提供了一类新型驱动激光。

title: Observation of quadrature-dependent unidirectional flow of light
abstract: Unidirectional transport of light is a central capability in photonics, enabling critical functionalities such as isolation and routing. Ordinarily, this directionality depends on the mode of light, but not its phase. In this work, we experimentally demonstrate phase-dependent unidirectional transport of light for the first time. Specifically, we realize a system where conjugate quadratures of an optical field decouple and propagate in opposite directions. Our all-optical approach uses multiple pump frequencies in a high-$Q$ nanophotonic micro-resonator to achieve Hamiltonian programming through Kerr nonlinearity. Even though we rely on optical nonlinearity, our approach is not limited to any minimal power requirement on the signal. We demonstrate the ultimate limit of this by measuring the effect of quadrature-dependent transport on vacuum fluctuations. Our approach unlocks a fundamental new capability for controlling light, and can enable previously inaccessible regimes of phase-sensitive directional amplification, sensing, and routing.

summaries.en: This work experimentally demonstrates phase-dependent unidirectional transport of light by using multiple pump frequencies in a high-Q nanophotonic micro-resonator to program the Hamiltonian via Kerr nonlinearity, such that conjugate quadratures of an optical field decouple and propagate in opposite directions, an effect observed even on vacuum fluctuations.
summaries.zh: 该工作通过在高Q值纳米光子微谐振器中使用多个泵浦频率，借助克尔非线性实现哈密顿量编程，使光场的共轭正交分量解耦并沿相反方向传播，从而首次实验演示了相位依赖的光单向传输，甚至观测到其对真空涨落的影响。
summaries.ja: 本研究は、高Q値ナノフォトニック微小共振器で複数のポンプ周波数を用い、カー非線形性によりハミルトニアンをプログラムすることで、光場の共役直交成分を分離して逆方向に伝搬させ、位相依存の光一方向輸送を初めて実験的に実証し、真空揺らぎへの影響まで観測した。

title: Dual deconvolution multifocal fluorescence response matrix microscopy for aberration-free high-throughput super-resolution imaging
abstract: Fluorescence response matrix imaging enables separate computational correction of excitation and emission aberrations through dual deconvolution, but single-focus acquisition requires a large number of camera frames, limiting its practical use. Multifocal excitation can accelerate acquisition by recording many illumination positions in parallel, but denser foci also increase inter-focus crosstalk, which can bias the estimated excitation and emission optical transfer functions and degrade aberration correction. Here, we introduce high-throughput aberration-free fluorescence response matrix imaging with adaptive multifocal illumination, in which the inter-focus spacing of the multifocal lattice is adjusted according to specimen-dependent crosstalk. A programmable digital micromirror device generates multifocal excitation lattices, and the resulting detector-resolved fluorescence responses are assembled into a two-coordinate fluorescence response matrix. Dual deconvolution separately estimates and corrects the excitation and emission optical transfer functions, and the aberration-corrected matrix is then combined in the spatial-frequency domain to reconstruct the aberration-free image. This strategy reduces the number of required camera frames by approximately three orders of magnitude, allowing response matrices with $\sim 10^6$ illumination positions to be acquired within seconds to a few minutes. The accelerated acquisition preserves the aberration-correction capability of dual deconvolution and achieves an estimated lateral resolution of $\sim$100 nm. Applied to heterogeneous mouse brain and kidney tissue, the method enables high-resolution, depth-resolved volumetric imaging while correcting specimen-dependent aberrations. Together, these results establish adaptive multifocal illumination as a practical route to high-throughput aberration-free fluorescence response matrix imaging.

summaries.en: Adaptive multifocal illumination with crosstalk-dependent focus spacing accelerates dual-deconvolution fluorescence response matrix imaging by about three orders of magnitude, enabling aberration-free volumetric super-resolution imaging of heterogeneous tissue at ~100 nm lateral resolution.

title: Comparative Robustness of Mach-Zehender and Microring Photonic Matrix Multipliers Under Laser RIN and Thermal Drift
abstract: Photonic matrix multipliers can accelerate neural-network inference, but their practical utility depends on how optical weight elements respond to source noise, thermal variation, and calibration error. This paper compares Mach-Zehnder modulator (MZM) and microring-resonator (MRR) implementations under laser relative-intensity noise (RIN), column-wise thermal/phase drift, and their joint action. Two CIFAR-10 classifiers - a compact four-layer CNN and ResNet-8 - are mapped to matched photonic multiply-accumulate chains using common source-distribution, detection, numerical, and calibration assumptions. Both architectures reproduce the same zero-perturbation baseline for each workload: 79.5% classification accuracy for the Small CNN and 70.0% for ResNet-8. Robustness is then evaluated using separate RIN-only and drift-only sweeps and a full two-dimensional RIN-drift grid, with dimensionless RMS perturbation levels extending from 0.5% to 20%. The analysis reports classification accuracy, class normalized confusion matrices, rolling-accuracy traces, one-dimensional robustness curves, and multidimensional response surfaces. Device equations and parameter definitions follow the models implemented in the QPI Labs Photonic Inference Simulator, with shared laser fluctuations propagated as correlated multiplicative noise and slow drift represented as a per-output-column perturbation of calibrated weights. All numerical results are generated from recorded experiment configurations and random seeds. The study provides a controlled system-level framework for comparing interferometric and resonant photonic weight elements while limiting conclusions to the implemented device models, perturbation ranges, calibration policy, and neural-network workloads.

summaries.en: This paper compares Mach-Zehnder modulator and microring-resonator photonic matrix multipliers for CIFAR-10 neural-network inference under laser relative-intensity noise, column-wise thermal/phase drift, and their combined effects, using matched simulation assumptions.
summaries.zh: 本文在激光相对强度噪声、列方向热/相位漂移及其联合作用下，比较了马赫-曾德尔调制器与微环谐振器光子矩阵乘法器用于CIFAR-10神经网络推理的表现，并采用匹配的仿真假设。

title: From Microresonator to Packaged Microcomb System: Fiber-Coupled Module and System Integration
abstract: We demonstrate a compact and robust soliton microcomb source designed for field-deployable operation. A directly fiber-coupled SiN microresonator was integrated with precise thermal control into a palm-sized module, reducing the footprint and volume by 16- and 81-fold, respectively. The module, together with the laser sources and optical amplifiers required for microcomb generation, was further integrated into a 19-inch rack-mounted enclosure, achieving system-level footprint and volume reductions of 2.3- and 3.7-fold, respectively. The packaged system achieved a 90% manual startup success rate and maintained continuous soliton operation for 18.8 days, while remaining operational under substantial temperature variations. A state-based automated startup scheme using discrete microcomb-state evaluation achieved single-soliton generation without manual intervention with success rates of 50% within 2 min and 60% within 3 min. Moreover, automated soliton initiation and sustained operation were demonstrated while the packaged microresonator module was directly subjected to random mechanical vibration. These results provide a practical platform for compact, robust, and field-deployable microcomb sources.

title: Tornado Wave-Encoded Point Spread Functions for Multi-Period Three-Dimensional Localization Imaging
abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) localization microscopy using rotational point spread functions (PSFs) is fundamentally challenged by limited axial range, poor PSF compactness, and depth-decoding ambiguity -- particularly in dense specimens with heavy PSF overlap. To address these limitations, we introduce a 3D localization approach based on tornado wave (ToW)-PSFs, combined with a convolutional neural network (CNN) designed to decode continuous rotational patterns and resolve multi-period axial ambiguity. Our engineered PSF encodes the 3D position of each nanoparticle into a compact double-lobe pattern whose orientation rotates with axial position. This design yields a clean, well-defined structural evolution across an unprecedented 15 um axial range, with an average rotation rate of 21.8 degrees/um, ensuring robust long-range depth encoding. To recover coordinates from overlapping emitters, we systematically benchmark a conventional matching-pursuit (MP) algorithm against our CNN. While MP performs adequately in sparse scenes, the CNN demonstrates exceptional robustness in dense fields, achieving a 70.24% localization accuracy at 20 particles per image-substantially outperforming MP's 22.52% -- while also significantly suppressing axial period-jump errors. Experimental validation on nanoparticles confirms reliable single- and multi-particle localization throughout the entire working range. Our results establish ToW-PSFs as a powerful and practical optical encoding strategy for high-density, extended-range 3D localization imaging.

title: Proposal for a multi-ion optical clock with hundreds of ions
abstract: Scaling trapped-ion optical clocks to hundreds of ions remains a major challenge due to inhomogeneous frequency shifts in large ion crystals. Here, we propose a circular surface-trap architecture for a multi-ion optical clock with hundreds of ions. The rotational symmetry of the ion crystal suppresses the main sources of inhomogeneity, quadrupole this http URL investigate the feasibility of a clock based on a ring crystal of 400 $^{40}\mathrm{Ca}^{+}$ ions and propose a suitable experimental setup configuration. We have shown that circular configuration of ions leads to suppression by two orders of magnitude of the quadrupole shift comparing to the linear trap. Combined with stray-field compensation and dynamical decoupling techniques, this architecture provides a pathway toward multi-ion optical clocks with fractional frequency uncertainty at the $10^{-18}$ level and an expected 20-fold improvement in frequency stability compared to single ion clocks.

summaries.en: A circular surface-trap architecture hosting a ring crystal of 400 40Ca+ ions is proposed for a multi-ion optical clock, where rotational symmetry suppresses the quadrupole shift by two orders of magnitude relative to a linear trap and, combined with stray-field compensation and dynamical decoupling, could reach 10^-18 fractional frequency uncertainty with a 20-fold stability improvement over single-ion clocks.

title: Intrinsic Orbital Nernst Effect in Real Photonic Bands
abstract: We predict an intrinsic orbital Nernst effect in reciprocal photonic lattices with real Bloch modes. In the collisionless regime, a thermal gradient generates a transverse angular-displacement response although band angular moments and ordinary Berry curvatures vanish. The response is carried by angular-density dipoles formed through virtual mixing of distinct spatial modes. Their correlation with band velocity survives thermal averaging and is independently recovered from the angular-density readout of unitarily evolved wave packets. Two controls expose the mechanism: a fixed-generator two-level system has zero antisymmetric intrinsic response, and flattening the dispersion suppresses transport without changing the eigenstates. A canonical scalar Maxwell calculation realizes the effect through symmetry-selected virtual channels, even when one band dominates the thermal population. These findings establish an orbital-dipole mechanism for intrinsic thermal angular transport in real photonic bands.

summaries.en: The paper predicts an intrinsic orbital Nernst effect in reciprocal photonic lattices with real Bloch modes, where a thermal gradient drives a transverse angular-displacement response carried by angular-density dipoles from virtual mode mixing, even when band angular moments and ordinary Berry curvatures vanish.
summaries.zh: 该论文预测了在具有实Bloch模态的互易光子晶格中存在内禀轨道能斯特效应，其中热梯度产生横向角位移响应，该响应由不同空间模态虚混合形成的角密度偶极子所携带，即使能带角矩和普通Berry曲率消失。
summaries.ja: 本論文は、実Blochモードを持つ相反光子格子において内在的軌道Nernst効果を予測する。

title: Nonperturbative optomechanics with thin, weakly reflective intracavity dielectrics
abstract: Levitated dielectric sensors are often treated as perturbative probes of a pre-existing optical field. We show that this picture fails for a novel sensor geometry: a dielectric plate whose transverse extent captures the full optical mode. Even an optically thin sensor with modest refractive index can heavily restructure the intracavity fields, effectively partitioning a cavity into two subcavities with substantial cross-coupling and producing new optical resonances and trapping sites with properties which deviate from the standard intuition. Conventional perturbative expressions for the cavity frequency shift and optomechanical coupling depart from the exact solution at thicknesses as small as $\sim\lambda/(10n)$. Furthermore, cavity locking decreases the coupling and increases the trap stiffness by orders of magnitude, and the coupled subcavity structure permits appreciable optical cooling at zero detuning, a distinct behavior unique to this nonperturbative regime. These effects, sharing a common origin, establish a distinct regime of cavity optomechanics in which the sensor is no longer merely a probe of the cavity field, but an element that helps define it.
subjects: Optics (physics.optics) ; Mesoscale and Nanoscale Physics (cond-mat.mes-hall); General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology (gr-qc); Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

summaries.en: A dielectric plate that spans the full optical mode can nonperturbatively restructure a cavity into coupled subcavities even when optically thin and weakly reflective, invalidating standard perturbative optomechanics and enabling unique effects such as optical cooling at zero detuning.
summaries.zh: 一块横向覆盖整个光学模式的介质板即使在光学薄且弱反射时也能非微扰地重构腔场，将腔分割为耦合的子腔，使标准微扰光力学的描述失效，并带来零失谐光学冷却等独特效应。
summaries.ja: 光学モード全体を覆う誘電体板は、光学的に薄く反射率が低くても非摂動的に共振器場を再構成して結合したサブ共振器に分割し、標準的な摂動光力学を無効にするとともにゼロ離調での光学冷却などの特有の効果を可能にする。

title: Direct growth of crack-free stoichiometric silicon nitride on sapphire for wide-band photonics
abstract: Low-loss stoichiometric silicon nitride on oxidized silicon has emerged as the major wide-band photonics platform for nonlinear and quantum photonics. These films, deposited by low-pressure chemical vapor deposition (LPCVD), are well known to have around 1000 MPa of residual tensile stress, which often leads to cracking when film thickness exceeds 400 nm. Although various stress-mitigation approaches can isolate or prevent cracking, this stress issue remains a major fabrication challenge. Low-residual-stress LPCVD stoichiometric silicon nitride on sapphire has also been reported and recently explored for photonics at telecommunication wavelengths. Here, we advance its development through systematic characterization, including thin-film stress analysis, ellipsometry and prism-coupling measurements of refractive index and loss, and swept-wavelength spectroscopy of fabricated photonic devices across a broad range of wavelengths. We demonstrate the direct growth of crack-free stoichiometric silicon nitride up to 2 {\mu}m thick with only 200 MPa of stress. Our fabricated devices show propagation losses of 0.35 dB/cm around 780 nm, 0.37 dB/cm around 1064 nm, and 0.25 dB/cm around 1630 nm. In addition, prism-coupling measurements indicate film losses below 1 dB/cm at wavelengths down to 500 nm. Our work highlights stoichiometric silicon nitride on sapphire as a promising wide-band photonics platform.

summaries.en: Direct growth of crack-free stoichiometric silicon nitride on sapphire achieves films up to 2 μm thick with only 200 MPa residual stress and low propagation losses across a wide wavelength range, establishing it as a promising wide-band photonics platform.

title: Photon-efficient readout of optical cavity arrays via spatial heterodyne
abstract: Optical cavity arrays are an emerging tool for efficiently interfacing optical photons to quantum emitters for applications such as quantum computing. In this work, we demonstrate a metrology technique for such cavity arrays by interfering cavity array outputs against a tilted reference beam on a camera, constituting a spatial heterodyne. Both the amplitude and phase of each cavity's transmitted field can be extracted from the resulting images. Enabled by the improved scaling of heterodyne detection over intensity detection in the presence of technical noise, we demonstrate signal-to-noise ratio greater than one down to the single detected photon level, even in the presence of hundreds of noise equivalent photons. This readout technique holds promise for fast, non-destructive imaging of atomic qubits in cavity arrays by requiring fewer scattered photons while allowing the use of fast cameras with higher electronic readout noise.

summaries.en: A spatial heterodyne technique that interferes cavity array outputs with a tilted reference beam on a camera enables photon-efficient readout of both amplitude and phase from each cavity, achieving signal-to-noise ratios above one down to the single-photon level even amidst hundreds of noise-equivalent photons.

title: Simultaneous Recovery of Dielectric Constants, Photoelastic Constants, and Strain Profiles from Picosecond Ultrasonic Echoes
abstract: Light reflected from a deforming solid depends on boundary motion and strain-induced modulation of the dielectric response. For a propagating acoustic field, scattering from different depths interferes coherently, so the measured optical amplitude and phase depend jointly on the strain profile, dielectric constant, and photoelastic constant. Optical tomography often makes such reconstructions tractable through independent projections. To probe mechanical strain, however, the optical measurement also depends on the material properties that mediate its observation, requiring those properties to be known or assumptions about the field. Here we show that broadband picosecond ultrasonic echoes in an opaque solid can supply the missing information. Fourier transformation of the measured complex relative reflectance change obtained with monochromatic light at normal incidence gives access to many acoustic frequency components. We recover the complex dielectric and photoelastic constants together with the nanoscale depth-dependent strain profile by formulating the reconstruction as a multiparameter nonlinear eigenvalue problem. We demonstrate the method using experimental echoes from a chromium film. The recovered refractive index agrees with ellipsometry, whereas the recovered strain profile closely follows a two-temperature-model prediction including electron and thermal diffusion and frequency-dependent ultrasonic attenuation. Synthetic echoes test robustness to added noise. Broadband response thus replaces additional optical projections, making the measurement self-calibrating and enabling simultaneous recovery of an unknown physical field and the material properties that mediate its optical observation.

summaries.en: Broadband picosecond ultrasonic echoes in an opaque solid enable simultaneous recovery of the complex dielectric and photoelastic constants and the nanoscale strain profile via a multiparameter nonlinear eigenvalue formulation, as demonstrated for a chromium film.
summaries.zh: 不透明固体中的宽带皮秒超声回波通过多参数非线性本征值公式化方法，可同时恢复复介电常数、光弹常数以及纳米级应变分布，并在铬膜上得到了验证。
summaries.ja: 不透明固体中の広帯域ピコ秒超音波エコーを用い、多パラメータ非線形固有値問題として定式化することで、複素誘電率と光弾性定数、およびナノスケールのひずみ分布を同時に復元でき、クロム薄膜で実証された。

title: Transfer learning-aided, artificial intelligence approach to evaluate optical properties of materials for classical and quantum photonic applications
abstract: In this study, an artificial intelligence-assisted evaluation of the refractive indices of different materials is performed. The evaluation of the refractive index is necessary to design photonic devices for various classical and quantum photonic applications, and to theoretically analyse experimental results. The refractive index is one of the crucial parameters that affect the interaction of light with matter. Although the refractive index can be measured experimentally, its estimation via computational means provide the advantage of not requiring costly instrumentation, trained researchers and could avoid potential laboratory-based uncertainties. Therefore, in this study, artificial intelligence is implemented to estimate the optical constants of two types of materials, i.e., noble metals, and semiconductors. To this end, an artificial neural network is used to estimate the real and the imaginary parts of the refractive index of a specific material for various wavelengths of light. Then, the knowledge of the trained neural network is employed to initiate and train new neural networks to estimate the refractive indices of other materials. For the training of a neural network, various methods can be deployed. However, the application of the training can be a time-consuming process. A transfer learning approach is here implemented to provide a faster training solution for the problem under study. The implementation of transfer learning allows training the neural networks for a new material with higher speed or accuracy when compared to non-knowledge transfer-based training. Our results show the efficiency of the proposed technique in accurately evaluating the real and imaginary parts of the refractive index of different materials.

summaries.en: This study uses transfer learning-based artificial neural networks to rapidly and accurately estimate the real and imaginary parts of the refractive index of noble metals and semiconductors, supporting classical and quantum photonic device design without costly experimental measurements.
summaries.zh: 本研究采用基于迁移学习的人工神经网络，快速准确地估算贵金属和半导体的折射率实部与虚部，从而无需昂贵的实验测量即可支持经典与量子光子器件的设计。
summaries.ja: 本研究では、転移学習を用いた人工ニューラルネットワークにより、貴金属および半導体の屈折率の実部と虚部を迅速かつ正確に推定し、高コストな実験測定を必要とせずに古典的・量子フォトニックデバイスの設計を支援する。

title: Quantum tomography of bright squeezed vacuum via strong-field ionization
abstract: Strong-field physics uses intense optical fields to probe and control electron motion on ultrafast timescales. Recent advances in bright squeezed vacuum have brought macroscopic quantum states of light into the ultrafast strong-field regime, opening prospects for high-harmonic generation and photoionization. Yet linking its phase-space structure to subcycle electron dynamics remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate strong-field tunneling ionization of xenon using a phase-referenced combination of coherent and squeezed fields, with the coherent field defining the ionization clock and quadrature fluctuations of the zero-mean squeezed field providing control. The squeezed field selectively modulates atomic tunneling barriers and electron wave packets, imprinting signatures on photoelectron momentum distributions, number statistics, and energy spectra. Using coincidence measurements of photon number and phase-sensitive photoelectron momentum distributions, we perform quantum state tomography of the driving field by reconstructing its Wigner function. These results establish a bidirectional interface between quantum optics and nonperturbative strong-field electron dynamics, in which the driving quantum field shapes subcycle electron motion while photoionization provides a phase-sensitive probe of the field's quantum state. This work opens new routes toward controlling electron dynamics with quantum light and phase-sensitive quantum state metrology through ultrafast strong-field electron dynamics.

summaries.en: Strong-field tunneling ionization of xenon driven by a phase-referenced combination of coherent and squeezed vacuum fields imprints the squeezed field's quadrature fluctuations on photoelectron momentum distributions and enables reconstruction of the driving field's Wigner function, establishing a bidirectional interface between quantum optics and nonperturbative strong-field electron dynamics.
summaries.zh: 利用相干场与压缩真空场的相位参考组合驱动氙原子的强场隧穿电离，压缩场的正交涨落被印刻在光电子动量分布上，并由此重建驱动场的维格纳函数，从而在量子光学与非微扰强场电子动力学之间建立起双向接口。
summaries.ja: コヒーレント場とスクイーズド真空場の位相参照結合によりキセノンの強場トンネルイオン化を駆動すると、スクイーズド場の直交位相揺らぎが光電子運動量分布に刻印され、駆動場のウィグナー関数を再構成できるため、量子光学と非摂動的強場電子ダイナミクスの双方向インターフェースが確立される。

title: Programmable spatiotemporal shaping for partially coherent structured wave packets
abstract: Providing more coherent light with space-time coupling offers unprecedented opportunities across diverse scientific disciplines and areas of technology. However, in many applications, tailored laser beams with partial coherence in space and time are desired. Here, we demonstrate a programmable approach for simultaneously shaping the intensity and coherence distributions of spatiotemporally coupled partially coherent wave packets. By jointly engineering the fractal speckle of a dynamic scatterer and applying tailored modulation of the illumination function, we experimentally generate partially coherent laser beams with arbitrarily designed intensity and nontrivial coherence distributions. The proposed approach is compatible with ultrafast laser pulses, enabling the on-demand generation of partially coherent space-time wave packets. The resulting spatiotemporally partially coherent wave packets exhibit non-separable space-time intensity profiles together with engineered spatiotemporal correlation distributions. This work provides a versatile framework for tailoring partially coherent light in space and time, with varied applications in relativistic laser-matter interaction, passive imaging and optical manipulation.

summaries.en: A programmable method jointly engineering a dynamic scatterer's fractal speckle and tailored illumination enables the experimental generation of partially coherent spatiotemporally coupled wave packets with arbitrarily designed intensity and nontrivial coherence distributions, including non-separable space-time intensity profiles and engineered spatiotemporal correlations that are compatible with ultrafast pulses.
summaries.zh: 通过联合调控动态散射体的分形散斑与定制照明调制，一种可编程方法实验生成了具有任意设计强度和非常规相干分布的部分相干时空耦合波包，其展现出不可分离的时空强度分布和工程化的时空关联，并兼容超快激光脉冲。
summaries.ja: 動的散乱体のフラクタルスペックルと調整された照明変調を組み合わせたプログラマブルな手法により、任意に設計された強度と非自明なコヒーレンス分布を持つ部分的にコヒーレントな時空間結合波束を実験的に生成し、非分離な時空間強度プロファイルと工学された時空間相関を示すとともに超高速レーザーパルスにも対応する。

title: High Sensitivity Transient Holographic Full-Polarization Microscopy
abstract: The polarization state of light provides direct access to ultrafast electronic, magnetic, and structural dynamics in materials. Transient wide-field microscopy with simultaneous amplitude, phase, and polarization sensitivity enables spatially resolved measurements of these dynamics, but its sensitivity is often limited by technical noise and background fluctuations. Here, we demonstrate transient holographic full-polarization microscopy with substantially reduced instrumental noise and sensitivity approaching the shot-noise limit. We compare holographic geometries using one, two, and four reference beams and find that the single-reference configuration provides the most favourable shot-noise-limited sensitivity for the derived polarization observables. Combined with two-camera detection, it simultaneously captures both orthogonal polarization components without distributing reference photons among multiple carriers. A self-referenced noise-reduction framework combining singular value decomposition and background subtraction further suppresses correlated noise. For spatially averaged regions, the baseline noise is reduced by factors of three-sixty, enabling detection of weaker transient responses at lower excitation densities and in weakly absorbing materials.

summaries.en: This paper demonstrates transient holographic full-polarization microscopy that achieves sensitivity approaching the shot-noise limit by using a single-reference-beam geometry with two-camera detection and a self-referenced noise-reduction framework, reducing baseline noise by a factor of three-hundred-sixty.
summaries.zh: 本文展示了瞬态全息全偏振显微术，通过采用单参考光束几何结构、双相机探测以及结合奇异值分解与背景减除的自参考降噪框架，使灵敏度接近散粒噪声极限，并将基线噪声降低至原来的三百六十分之一。
summaries.ja: 本論文は、単一参照光束の光学配置と2台のカメラによる検出、および特異値分解と背景減算を組み合わせた自己参照ノイズ低減フレームワークを用いることで、ショットノイズ限界に近い感度を達成し、ベースラインノイズを360分の1に低減する過渡ホログラフィック全偏光顕微鏡を実証した。

title: Fading Memory and Nonlinear Dynamics in a Microring Resonator Network and their Use in Computation
abstract: Silicon microring resonators are promising components for photonic reservoir computing because their nonlinear optical response can transform signals and retain information about recent inputs. Under constant optical excitation, their coupled free-carrier and thermal dynamics can generate self-pulsing: a periodic output response. However, constant-input behavior does not reveal how these dynamics respond to randomly modulated signals or whether their memory is useful for temporal processing. Here, we characterize a single silicon microring resonator and a passive network of microring resonators under random input modulation. The temporal component associated with self-pulsing remains observable under random modulation, but the largest fading memory occurs near the self-pulsing boundary, where no resolved self-pulsing-like oscillation is present. reservoir computing metrics, such as memory capacity, map this accessible memory, and its decay provides effective timescales associated mainly with free-carrier and thermal relaxation. Finally, we use NARMA reconstruction to test whether the measured memory profile supports nonlinear temporal processing. Responses with a resolved self-pulsing-like component perform worse on this task, and the intrinsic memory profile is not matched to the required input history. These results show that reservoir computing metrics can characterize nonlinear microring resonator dynamics even when the physical system is not an effective standalone reservoir for the selected task.

summaries.en: Random-input modulation of a silicon microring resonator and a passive microring network shows that the largest fading memory occurs near the self-pulsing boundary without resolved self-pulsing oscillations, and that reservoir computing metrics can characterize these nonlinear free-carrier and thermal dynamics even though the memory profile performs worse on NARMA reconstruction when a resolved self-pulsing-like component is present.
summaries.zh: 对单个硅微环谐振器及无源微环谐振器网络施加随机输入调制的研究表明，最大的衰落记忆出现在自脉冲边界附近，此时不存在可分辨的自脉冲类振荡，并且储层计算指标能够刻画这些由自由载流子和热弛豫主导的非线性动力学，尽管当存在可分辨的自脉冲类成分时该记忆特性在NARMA重构任务上表现更差。
summaries.ja: 単一シリコン微小リング共振器および受動微小リング共振器ネットワークにランダム入力変調を加えた研究により、最大のフェーディングメモリは分解可能な自励発振様振動が存在しない自励発振境界付近で生じ、自由キャリアと熱緩和に主に起因する非線形ダイナミクスをリザバーコンピューティング指標で特徴付けられるが、分解可能な自励発振様成分が存在する場合にはそのメモリプロファイルはNARMA再構成でより悪い性能を示すことが明らかになった。

title: Asynchronous Terahertz-field sampling with soliton microcombs
abstract: Terahertz time-domain spectroscopy records the electric field of terahertz transients and underpins applications from materials science to non-destructive testing. Asynchronous optical sampling enables systems without moving parts, but its acquisition rate remains fundamentally limited by the repetition-rate of the driving femtosecond lasers. Here, we demonstrate asynchronous terahertz-field sampling with two chip-based soliton microcombs. Their ultrahigh 25 GHz pulse repetition-rate drastically reduces dead-time during acquisition, and stabilization via sideband injection-locking enables coherent averaging without active feedback loops. At 10 kHz acquisition rate, we achieve a dynamic range of 74 dB in a single 100 $\mu$s scan, and 100 dB after 50 ms of coherent averaging with a 1.6 THz bandwidth. Acquisition rates of up to 100 kHz are demonstrated, limited only by detection electronics. Together with a proof-of-concept silicon wafer thickness measurement, these results establish soliton microcombs as compact sources for rapid terahertz-field sampling.

summaries.en: Asynchronous terahertz-field sampling using two chip-based soliton microcombs with a 25 GHz repetition rate achieves a 74 dB dynamic range in a single 100 µs scan and 100 dB after 50 ms coherent averaging over 1.

title: Cavity-modified static polarizabilities of atoms and small molecules within QED full configuration interaction
abstract: Static dipole polarizabilities of H$_2$, LiH, and helium confined in a single-mode optical cavity are computed using quantum-electrodynamical full configuration interaction (QED-FCI). Response properties are obtained as finite-field derivatives of the coupled electron-photon energy. The cavity-induced modification is found to arise from the competition of two contributions of opposite sign, the dipole self-energy and photon exchange, whose relative strength depends on both the cavity frequency and the number of photons involved in the exchange. The residual change suppresses the response of the molecular ground electronic states. For the metastable states of helium atom this balance changes qualitatively, and the differential response of the $2\,^3S_1 \to 2\,^1S_0$ clock transition, which governs its sensitivity to static electric fields and to thermal radiation, is strongly enhanced instead. Cavity confinement can therefore either reduce or increase the dc Stark and blackbody-radiation shifts of a frequency standard, depending on the electronic structure of the states involved. The reported data serve as a reference for cavity-modified response and underscore the need for an exact treatment of light-matter correlation in cavity-QED predictions.

summaries.en: Using QED full configuration interaction, static dipole polarizabilities of H2, LiH, and helium in a single-mode optical cavity are shown to be modified by competing dipole self-energy and photon-exchange contributions, which suppress the response of molecular ground states but strongly enhance the differential response of helium's 2 3S1 to 2 1S0 clock transition.
summaries.zh: 采用量子电动力学全组态相互作用计算表明，单模光学腔中H2、LiH和氦的静态偶极极化率受到偶极自能与光子交换两种相反贡献竞争的影响，从而抑制分子基态的响应，却强烈增强氦原子2 3S1到2 1S0钟跃迁的差分响应。
summaries.ja: 量子電磁力学完全配置間相互作用を用いた計算により、単一モード光共振器内のH2、LiH、ヘリウムの静的双極子分極率は、双極子自己エネルギーと光子交換という逆符号の二つの寄与の競合により変化し、分子基底状態の応答を抑制する一方、ヘリウム原子の2 3S1→2 1S0時計遷移の微分応答を強く増強することが示された。

title: Wireless Energy Transfer for Space Applications: A Review of Technologies, Mission Architectures, Energy Routing, and System Integration
abstract: Wireless energy transfer (WET) decouples energy generation from energy use, offering strategic advantages for distributed spacecraft, lunar surface networks, mobile assets, and high-power remote loads. This review organizes the field along four axes: physical mechanism, energy reference plane, mission architecture, and evidence maturity. It examines near field inductive and resonant transfer, microwave and millimeter wave power beaming, optical and laser-based transfer, space-based solar power, lunar and cislunar energy delivery, inter-spacecraft power sharing, intraspacecraft contactless interfaces, and reconfigurable or relay assisted routing within a common R0,R7 energy-accounting framework. Three conclusions emerge. First, WET is most valuable when spatial or temporal mismatches separate energy generation from load demand; it does not universally replace local generation or onboard storage. Second, dominant losses vary across system architectures. Beam collection, rectification, receiver output, and useful load efficiencies are therefore not directly comparable without explicitly defined energy reference planes. Third, technological maturity is uneven. High power ground demonstrations and short range flight applications are relatively well established, whereas long-range radiative inter spacecraft transfer, spaceborne routing hardware, lunar energy networks, and deep space applications remain supported primarily by models, simulations, and mission studies rather than hardware demonstrations. Progress requires validated end to end energy budgets under mission realistic constraints, including pointing and tracking, thermal management, environmental exposure, reliability, energy storage, and regulatory compliance.

summaries.en: This review organizes wireless energy transfer for space applications across four axes—physical mechanism, energy reference plane, mission architecture, and evidence maturity—within a common energy-accounting framework, concluding that WET is most valuable when spatial or temporal mismatches separate generation from load, that dominant losses and efficiency comparisons depend on explicitly defined energy reference planes, and that maturity is uneven, with high-power ground demonstrations and short-range flight established while long-range radiative transfer, spaceborne routing, lunar networks, and deep-space applications remain largely model- and study-based.
summaries.zh: 本综述以物理机制、能量参考平面、任务架构和证据成熟度四个维度，在统一能量核算框架下梳理空间应用无线能量传输，结论指出：当发电与负载需求存在空间或时间错配时WET最具价值，主导损耗因系统架构而异、效率比较需明确定义能量参考平面，且技术成熟度不均——高功率地面演示与短距离飞行应用相对成熟，而长距离辐射式航天器间传输、星载路由硬件、月球能源网络和深空应用仍主要依赖模型、仿真与任务研究。
summaries.ja: 本レビューは、物理機構・エネルギー基準面・ミッションアーキテクチャ・証拠成熟度の4軸に沿って宇宙応用向け無線エネルギー伝送を共通のエネルギー会計枠組みで整理し、発電と負荷需要の空間的・時間的ミスマッチがある場合にWETが最も有用であること、主要損失はシステム構成ごとに異なり効率比較には明示的なエネルギー基準面の定義が必要であること、高功率の地上実証や短距離飛行応用は比較的成熟している一方で長距離放射型の宇宙機間伝送・宇宙搭載ルーティング・月面エネルギー網・深宇宙応用は主にモデル・シミュレーション・ミッション研究に支えられているという不均一な成熟度を結論づける。

title: Image Priors for Single-Shot Coded Diffraction Phase Retrieval
abstract: Phase retrieval recovers complex-valued objects from intensity-only measurements. In its classical Fourier form, reconstruction suffers from twin-image stagnation. Coded diffraction imaging, which adds a random phase mask before the Fourier transform, has so far required several masks. We show that an image prior makes single-shot coded diffraction imaging possible, with a single random mask followed by a Fourier transform. We validate this claim in simulation and in an optical experiment, in which a spatial light modulator displays the phase object together with the random mask. Our experimental validation covers five test signals and 530 images from the public Brno quantitative phase microscopy dataset of five adherent cell lines. With no image prior or with Fourier-only measurements, reconstruction of complex-valued objects from a single diffraction pattern consistently fails. An out-of-the-box pretrained image denoiser enables accurate reconstruction, in simulation even with fewer measurements than unknowns. Five regularization frameworks built on the same denoiser and one learned weakly convex regularizer all reconstruct the experimental images with peak signal-to-noise ratios within one decibel of each other. A single random phase mask and image priors thus turn coded diffraction imaging into a practical single-shot modality for quantitative phase imaging.

summaries.en: An image prior enables single-shot coded diffraction phase retrieval, allowing accurate reconstruction of complex-valued objects from a single diffraction pattern with one random phase mask and a Fourier transform, as validated in simulations and optical experiments on quantitative phase microscopy images.
summaries.zh: 图像先验使得单次编码衍射相位恢复成为可能，仅需一个随机相位掩模和傅里叶变换即可从单幅衍射图样中准确重建复值物体，并在定量相位显微图像模拟与光学实验中得到验证。
summaries.ja: 画像事前分布により、単一のランダム位相マスクとフーリエ変換を用いた単発符号化回折位相回復が可能となり、複素値物体の正確な再構成がシミュレーションと定量的位相顕微鏡画像の光学実験で検証された。

title: Chiral Vector Beams for Topological Enantio-Sensitive Imaging
abstract: Molecular chiral discrimination is vital across chemistry and life sciences, yet optical approaches remain highly inefficient for small organic molecules. Here we turn vector beams, whose polarization carries a topological charge, into an efficient probe of molecular handedness. We show that the combination of a tightly focused radially polarized beam at the fundamental frequency {\omega} and an azimuthally polarized beam at 2{\omega} creates chiral vector beams, a locally chiral field with structured handedness. Using state-of-the-art computational modeling in the chiral molecule carvone, we show that the nonlinear response (notably sum-frequency generation) of randomly oriented chiral molecules to this chiral vector beam captures the fields' local handedness and is highly enantio-sensitive. The two enantiomers emit light at frequency 3{\omega} with topological ring structures of different divergence, and thus the molecular handedness can be read out directly from the ring radius. The signal inherits the Poincaré index of the driving field, opening up new ways to robust, ultrafast, and and all-optical chiral discrimination.

summaries.en: Tightly focusing a radially polarized fundamental beam with an azimuthally polarized second-harmonic beam creates a locally chiral vector field whose sum-frequency generation in randomly oriented chiral molecules yields enantio-sensitive 3ω emission with topological ring structures whose radius directly encodes molecular handedness.
summaries.zh: 将紧聚焦的径向偏振基频光束与方位角偏振的二倍频光束结合，可产生局部手性矢量场，其在随机取向的手性分子中的和频产生会生成对映体敏感的3ω发射，并带有拓扑环结构，其半径直接编码了分子手性。
summaries.ja: 強く集光した動径偏光の基本波ビームと方位角偏光の第二高調波ビームを組み合わせることで局所的にキラルなベクトル場が生成され、ランダム配向したキラル分子における和周波発生は、分子の handedness を直接反映する半径を持つトポロジカルなリング構造を伴うエナンチオ感受性の3ω放射を生み出す。

title: Programmable Hard-X-Ray Spectral Comb Generation via Laser-Compton Scattering
abstract: Independent control of line spacing and offset underpins programmable frequency-comb spectroscopy, yet it has not been established for hard-X-ray sources based on inverse Compton scattering after electron transport and angular collection. Self-consistent multi-particle tracking and Li'enard-Wiechert radiation calculations model a transported 10 pC beam and its angle-integrated spectrum near 11 keV. Laser pulse separation programs the comb spacing, while pulse-to-pulse phase translates the entire line grid at fixed spacing. The spacing model agrees within 0.52%, while transport and optics change the phase-transfer slope by less than 0.2%. At fixed electron spot size, the largest resolvable separation scales as the inverse square of normalized emittance; subnanometer bunches also produce a mode-locked train with 13.9 as spacing. This two-coordinate programmability enables phase-stepped multicolor measurements and offers routes to hard-X-ray Ramsey interferometry, coherent control of core and nuclear excitations, and attosecond nonlinear spectroscopy.

summaries.en: This work demonstrates that laser pulse separation sets the hard-X-ray spectral comb spacing while pulse-to-pulse phase shifts the entire line grid at fixed spacing, enabling programmable hard-X-ray frequency combs via inverse Compton scattering.
summaries.zh: 这项工作表明，激光脉冲间隔决定硬X射线光谱梳的间距，而脉冲间相位在固定间距下平移整个谱线栅格，从而通过逆康普顿散射实现可编程的硬X射线频率梳。
summaries.ja: 本研究は、レーザーパルス間隔が硬X線スペクトルコムの間隔を決め、パルス間位相が固定間隔でスペクトル線格子全体を平行移動させることを示し、逆コンプトン散乱によるプログラマブルな硬X線周波数コムを実現する。

title: Principles and Techniques for Agentic Research in Experimental Physics
abstract: The use of artificial intelligence (AI) in physics research is increasingly common, yet few guidelines exist for its effective use. Starting with a principles-based approach, we outline a set of ten requirements for collaborative AI agents in experimental physics, spanning scientific norms, effective agent use, and domain expertise. We take a human-centered approach in which agents act as collaborators that amplify rather than replace the expertise of a human researcher (user) who directs the work and is responsible for its results. We then present a framework designed to enforce these requirements, detailing methods for improving off-the-shelf behavior of large language models (LLMs) with custom scaffolding and describing general-purpose scientific workflows and skills. In particular, we highlight the power of closed-loop campaigns where agents work iteratively toward a well-defined goal. We demonstrate the potential of this mode of research through six case studies in experimental physics, covering device design, hardware control, neural network optimization, physical model identification, and data analysis. All six case studies result in useful work products that add utility to our research, including a neural network architecture and solid-state quantum defect photodynamic model that substantially outperform our published work; a microwave waveguide design that extends a published design concept to a fabrication-ready device meeting our experimental constraints; a quantum control pulse sequence candidate that improves simulated performance by more than an order of magnitude; commissioning of an NMR spectrometer to $\sim$1~Hz frequency precision on live hardware; and finally a data-fitting pipeline that achieves, to our knowledge, the first reconstruction of the Ising microstate of an artificial spin-ice array from diffraction-limited magnetic imaging.

summaries.en: This paper presents ten requirements and a closed-loop framework for AI agents in experimental physics that amplify human expertise, demonstrated through six case studies spanning device design, hardware control, neural network optimization, physical model identification, and data analysis, several of which substantially outperform prior published results.
summaries.zh: 本文提出了实验物理学中协作式人工智能代理的十项要求和一个闭环框架，旨在增强而非取代人类研究者的专业知识，并通过涵盖器件设计、硬件控制、神经网络优化、物理模型识别和数据分析的六个案例研究加以验证，其中多项成果显著优于此前已发表的工作。
summaries.ja: 本論文は、実験物理学における協働型AIエージェントのための10の要件と閉ループ型フレームワークを提示し、人間の研究者の専門性を代替ではなく増幅することを目指して、デバイス設計、ハードウェア制御、ニューラルネットワーク最適化、物理モデル同定、データ解析にわたる6つのケーススタディで実証し、そのうち複数が既発表の成果を大幅に上回った。

title: Observation of Photon Bunching in Broadband Multimode Thermal Light Enabled by Temporal Imaging
abstract: Photons emitted by incoherent sources exhibit temporal bunching, a fundamental manifestation of Bose-Einstein statistics first observed by Hanbury Brown and Twiss (HBT). While intensity correlation measurements originated in astronomy and are now central across quantum technologies, biophysics, and spectroscopy, observing temporal bunching in broadband thermal light remains limited by detector temporal resolution. Conventional approaches - such as streak cameras or optical upconversion - introduce severe trade-offs in efficiency, bandwidth, or setup versatility. Here, we propose and demonstrate a third route: pre-detection temporal magnification of the optical field prior to measuring its intensity autocorrelation function in a conventional HBT setup. Using an electro-optic time lens with a temporal magnification of 660, we resolve the temporal intensity autocorrelation of broadband thermal light generated via non-degenerate spontaneous parametric down-conversion with a bandwidth of 250 GHz. This enables direct observation of thermal photon bunching on sub-3.5 picosecond timescales without narrow spectral filtering, establishing pre-detection temporal imaging as a general platform for broadband statistical optics, with applications spanning ultrafast quantum optics, biophysical imaging, and potentially stellar intensity interferometry.

title: Progress in Cavitated Front Gridline Ag Paste for PERC Solar Cell Architecture
abstract: This paper reports on the progress made with the cavitated silver paste on passivated emitter rear contact cells (PERC) to reduce the series resistance. Thus, electrical and microscopy characterizations are used to examine these resistive losses. Fifteen 252 cm2 PERC cells were fabricated for this assessment. Under standard test conditions, these cells achieved a mean conversion efficiency of 21.87% and a maximum of 22.07%. The mean measured fill factor was 79.98%, compared with a pseudo-fill factor of 83.60%, giving a mean deficit of 3.62 percentage points. Fill factor decreased with increasing area-normalized series resistance, which ranged from 0.53 to 0.83 ohm-cm2, while open-circuit voltage and short-circuit current remained unvaried. These electrical trends support resistive current extraction as the principal contributor to fill-factor variation. Electroluminescence imaging revealed localized emission nonuniformity. Cross-sectional scanning transmission electron microscopy showed variation in the glass interfacial layer, while scanning electron microscopy identified micrometer and sub micrometer silver particles. Conductive atomic force microscopy after sequential removal of the bulk metal and glass revealed spatially heterogeneous current response. These observations are consistent with nonuniform electrical access at the contact, where restricted conducting pathways may concentrate on current and increase local voltage drops. The combined characterization identifies interfacial heterogeneity and the connectivity of conducting pathways as priorities for understanding and reducing extraction losses in cavitated silver metallization.

title: Zeptosecond-level timing-noise floor in optical-to-terahertz photomixing
abstract: Optical generation of terahertz (0.1 to 10\,THz) carriers can, in principle, preserve the spectral purity of an optical reference without the noise penalty associated with electronic frequency multiplication. Here, we identify and suppress the dominant excess-noise mechanisms that limit this conversion in high-power uni-travelling-carrier photodiodes. We characterize amplitude-to-phase conversion as functions of photocurrent and reverse bias and identify operating parameters to minimize the effect. We quantify the white phase noise introduced by optical amplification and show that this contribution can be eliminated by directly driving the photodiode with a high-power optical source. With the excess noise mitigated, we use cross-correlation phase-noise measurements to observe a white phase-noise floor of $-161.0$~dBc/Hz at 263.2~GHz, corresponding to a timing-noise floor of 7.6~zs/$\sqrt{\mathrm{Hz}}$. The remaining floor follows the photocurrent dependence expected from shot noise. Extending the measurement across the full WR-3.4 band, from 220 to 330~GHz, yields timing-noise floors below 10~zs/$\sqrt{\mathrm{Hz}}$ throughout, with a minimum of 6.0~zs/$\sqrt{\mathrm{Hz}}$. These results establish direct photomixing as a route to sub-10-zs/$\sqrt{\mathrm{Hz}}$ white timing-noise floors for continuous-wave sources at terahertz frequencies and identify the noise processes that must be controlled to reach this regime.

summaries.en: By identifying and suppressing amplitude-to-phase conversion and optical-amplification noise in high-power uni-travelling-carrier photodiodes, cross-correlation phase-noise measurements reveal a white phase-noise floor of -161.

title: An Aubry-André localized optical lattice clock
abstract: Optical lattice clocks in space could improve satellite navigation systems and enable new tests of fundamental physics, including gravitational-wave detection and tests of relativity. In microgravity, atoms can tunnel to degenerate neighboring lattice sites, broadening the clock transition and limiting coherence times. We demonstrate Aubry-André localization in a bichromatic optical lattice formed by two magic-wavelength lasers, suppressing tunneling in a horizontal lattice clock emulating free fall. We recover a Fourier-limited clock Rabi spectrum and measure Ramsey coherence times of up to 2 s in shallow lattices, with up to 100-fold improvement over the delocalized regime. These results establish Aubry-André localization as a practical route to controlling tunneling in future space-based clocks, and open a path to operating terrestrial clocks at shallower lattice depths.

summaries.en: Aubry-André localization in a bichromatic magic-wavelength optical lattice suppresses tunneling in a horizontal lattice clock, restoring a Fourier-limited Rabi spectrum and Ramsey coherence times up to 2 s, about 100 times better than in the delocalized regime.

title: Non-contact lens metrology from optical flow and differentiable ray tracing
abstract: Accurate lens surface metrology is essential to determine the manufactured geometry of refractive optical elements and their deviation from the specified design. We demonstrate a transmission metrology method that reconstructs refractive lens surfaces from the displacement of a wavelet-noise-patterned mask. Lens-induced distortion is represented by a dense displacement field. A differentiable ray tracer fits the lens geometry using a calibrated near-telecentric camera model with an effective finite ray origin. We validate the method on commercial lenses. The recovered geometries agree with nominal specifications, and the plano-aspheric reconstruction is compared with chromatic confocal profilometry.

title: Inverse design of poles and zeros: tailoring phase control in metasurfaces
abstract: We develop a physically interpretable inverse-design framework for generalized Huygens metasurfaces, using prescribed scattering poles and zeros to engineer resonance interference and transmission-phase control. Compared with direct optimization of transmission or reflection coefficients, this approach offers a physically transparent route to rationally controlling resonance properties, including linewidth and group delay, while reducing computational cost. The resulting designs demonstrate how near-unity transmission and $2\pi$ phase excursion can arise from resonance interference. These signatures of the Kerker effect extend beyond the conventional alignment of electric and magnetic dipole resonances to other mechanisms, including guided-mode resonances and quasi-bound states in the continuum. We further optimize the Kerker condition across a continuum of refractive-index states in a reconfigurable phase change material metasurface, enabling high-transmission $2\pi$ phase tuning. Our results establish a versatile and practical approach to metasurface phase control through the targeted design of scattering poles and zeros.

summaries.en: A physically interpretable inverse-design framework for generalized Huygens metasurfaces uses prescribed scattering poles and zeros to engineer resonance interference and transmission-phase control, achieving near-unity transmission with 2π phase excursion and enabling high-transmission phase tuning in a reconfigurable phase-change metasurface.

title: Practical Mid-infrared Dual-comb Spectroscopy with Absolute Frequency Referencing Based on a Single-cavity Dual-comb Fiber Laser
abstract: We demonstrate a practical mid-infrared (MIR) dual-comb spectroscopy (DCS) method based on a bidirectional dual-comb fiber laser. By exploiting the inherently high relative stability and mutual coherence of the dual-comb laser, we stabilize the MIR dual-comb modes with sufficient precision using only piezoelectric control of the repetition frequencies. This simple configuration enables correction of residual timing jitter and phase noise in interferograms while preserving the absolute optical frequency scale defined by the experimentally obtained comb parameters, without requiring an external continuous-wave laser reference or tight phase-locking. Importantly, the proposed method does not merely produce apparently clean interferograms through signal processing, but enables coherent averaging while retaining both the physically meaningful interferometric waveforms and well-defined absolute frequency information. The proposed system is experimentally validated through MIR spectroscopy of N$_2$O around 3.9 $\mu$m, achieving a signal-to-noise ratio of approximately 690 through coherent averaging of 10,000 interferograms over 65 s, along with the acquisition of an absorption spectrum consistent with the reference data. These results demonstrate a simple and practical approach to absolute-frequency-referenced MIR-DCS.

title: Theory of deeply subwavelength electromagnetic structuring of semiconductors due to thermal-ionization instability
abstract: We develop a theory of ionization-assisted instability that governs the reflection of intense electromagnetic pulses from a semiconductor surface. Local overheating of the material increases the free-carrier density and conductivity, which in turn enhances the absorption of the incident radiation and further amplifies local heating and avalanche ionization. At high pump repetition rates, the overheating accumulates from pulse to pulse, leading to a gradual rise of the local material temperature and free carrier density - a positive feedback loop that drives thermal runaway. However, this effect competes with diffraction of the pump field on the emerging perturbation of the dielectric permittivity or on the surface relief, which reduces the local electric field amplitude in the overheated regions, thus providing negative feedback. We show that the competition between heat diffusion and diffraction near-field weakening creates conditions for the exponential growth of temperature perturbations with a certain wavenumber determined by the pulse repetition rate, pump field, thermal conductivity and other material parameters. The derived analytical expressions accurately describe the spatial period of deeply subwavelength structures observed in recent experiments on silicon structuring by intense terahertz radiation, and reproduce qualitatively dependencies of their period on the pump intensity, the incident wavelength and the number of pump pulses.

summaries.en: A theory of thermal-ionization instability explains how intense electromagnetic pulses create deeply subwavelength periodic structures on semiconductor surfaces through a competition between positive thermal feedback from avalanche ionization and negative feedback from diffraction-induced near-field weakening.

title: On-chip optical isolators
abstract: Optical isolation suppresses back-reflections that destabilize lasers, produce parasitic interference, and increase crosstalk in photonic systems. Although free-space and fibre-optic isolators are mature, no broadly adopted on-chip technology yet combines strong isolation, low insertion loss, broad bandwidth, compact footprint, and scalable fabrication. The difficulty is twofold: Lorentz reciprocity must be broken, and every relevant backward spatial, spectral, and polarization channel must be suppressed. This Review develops a common framework for assessing proposed solutions. We first distinguish pairwise nonreciprocity from intensity-asymmetric transmission and from true isolation using the constitutive relations and scattering matrix. We then compare three physical routes to an integrated nonreciprocal response: magneto-optical bias, externally driven space-time modulation, and nonlinear optical processes. Topological and non-Hermitian systems are treated as cross-cutting design frameworks that can route, protect, or enhance an underlying nonreciprocal response, but do not by themselves break reciprocity. Finally, we examine fundamental constraints and practical trade-offs among isolation, insertion loss, bandwidth, footprint, modal coverage, drive requirements, and fabrication compatibility. The resulting mechanism-based perspective connects reciprocity-breaking physics to the requirements of scalable photonic integrated circuits.

summaries.en: This review develops a unified framework for assessing on-chip optical isolators by distinguishing pairwise nonreciprocity from intensity-asymmetric transmission and true isolation through constitutive relations and scattering matrices, comparing magneto-optical bias, externally driven space-time modulation, and nonlinear optical processes as physical routes to break reciprocity, while treating topological and non-Hermitian systems as cross-cutting design frameworks that can route, protect, or enhance an underlying nonreciprocal response but do not by themselves break reciprocity.

title: A Photonic Integrated Light Generation, Control, and Delivery Engine for Creating Cold Atoms
abstract: The creation of cold atoms underpins quantum sensing and precision metrology, computing, timekeeping, and fundamental science experiments. Miniaturizing the lasers and optical infrastructure, which occupy over 80% of the volume of these experiments, through photonic integration could improve robustness, reliability, and manufacturability while reducing cost and enabling portable space-based precision measurements and quantum tools for non-experts. Yet, there has been limited progress towards integration of the laser and optical infrastructure required to generate cold atoms onto a single chip. We demonstrate a photonic engine that generates, controls, and delivers precision light to create cold atoms in a rubidium 3-dimensional magneto-optical trap (3D-MOT). We integrate on a single chip two frequency-agile self-injection-locked lasers, laser frequency and intensity control, passive beam combining and splitting, signal monitoring, and high-efficiency beam delivery to a rubidium vapor cell. The integrated engine is shown to support multiple functions required for generating cold atoms including stable generation of low-noise cooling and repump light, frequency control for atom spectroscopy and stabilization, real-time laser monitoring, routing for laser offset locking, optical power modulation, and large-area three-beam delivery of 3 mW to the physics package. Fully electrically controlled, the engine enables sustained 3D-MOT operation, trapping more than 1 million atoms at an average temperature of 350 uK and supporting atom-number and temperature measurements. These results demonstrate the first single-chip integration of light generation, control, and delivery for cold-atom generation, offering a path toward smaller, more robust, and manufacturable cold-atom systems for applications including cold-atom clocks and sensors.

summaries.en: A single-chip photonic engine that integrates frequency-agile self-injection-locked lasers, optical control, and beam delivery generates and sustains a rubidium 3D magneto-optical trap with over 1 million atoms at 350 uK, marking the first single-chip integration of light generation, control, and delivery for cold-atom creation.

title: Recovery-Oriented Optical System Design Based on Fisher Information
abstract: Traditional optical system design for imaging applications has long been guided by image quality metrics such as geometrical RMS spot size, wavefront error, and modulation transfer function (MTF). Although these metrics effectively characterize direct imaging performance, they do not necessarily indicate optimal behavior when image restoration is subsequently applied. In modern imaging pipelines, however, optical systems are increasingly combined with physics-based or learning-based restoration methods, making the information transfer properties of the optical system critically important. In this work, we propose a recovery-oriented optical design approach that explicitly links optical system optimization with image restoration performance through an estimation-theoretic framework based on Fisher information. A new design criterion is adopted to ensure that the information encoded by the optical system can be reliably recovered during image restoration. To validate the proposed approach, two dual separated aspheric lenses are designed under identical configurations using conventional RMS-based optimization and the proposed recovery-oriented optimization, respectively. Although the RMS-optimized lens exhibits superior direct imaging quality, it underperforms after image restoration compared to the recovery-oriented design. These results demonstrate that recovery-oriented optical design provides a physically interpretable and effective extension of traditional optical design criteria for imaging systems operating within modern computational imaging pipelines.

summaries.en: This paper proposes a recovery-oriented optical design method that optimizes optical systems based on Fisher information to ensure that the encoded information can be reliably recovered during image restoration, and demonstrates that a lens designed with this criterion outperforms a conventionally RMS-optimized lens after restoration.

title: Chirality Inversion and Giant Optical Activity in Scalable Self-Assembled Metamaterials
abstract: Chiral materials manipulate light in ways that hold promise for sensing, imaging, and photonics, but producing such materials with strong and reproducible optical activity at large scale remains challenging. Here, we develop a scalable strategy to assemble hierarchical helicoidal metamaterials from metallic nanoparticles and chitin nanocrystals, a biosourced polysaccharide. Spontaneous co-assembly produces ordered chiral structures with strong plasmonic optical activity, reaching a dissymmetry factor of 0.55. The unprecedented ability to vary the helicoidal pitch allows control of the optical response, enabling inversion of optical handedness without changing the handedness of the template, effectively decoupling geometrical chirality from optical chirality. Remarkably, the gold nanoparticles can also be recovered from dry films and redispersed as colloids, introducing an appealing circularity concept for sustainable chiral plasmonic materials.

title: Experimental Demonstration of 7-Dimensional N-Vector Model with Dimensional Inflation and Annealing
abstract: We report the first experimental realization of a physical system described by a high-dimensional Hamiltonian comprising up to seven dimensions. Our setup is based on a holographic optical computer, which realizes a dimensional inflation by spatial and temporal multiplexing of lower dimensional systems. We demonstrate an $N$-vector model, with applications in field theory and computing. The approach is scalable and enables table-top implementation of high-dimensional theoretical models, and novel methods for combinatorial optimization. We experimentally demonstrate dimensional annealing: by dynamically reducing the number of dimensions, the ground state of an Ising model is found in complex graphs by an adiabatic evolution from high-dimensional spaces.

summaries.en: A holographic optical computer experimentally realizes a seven-dimensional N-vector model through spatial and temporal multiplexing of lower-dimensional systems, enabling dimensional inflation and adiabatic dimensional annealing to find Ising ground states in complex graphs.
